items.title: Cyclone Arnab impact on Andhra: Seven dead, CM Naidu estimates Rs 4600 crore loss
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu visited cyclone-affected areas in the state in the aftermath of Cyclone Arnab, which made landfall along the state’s coast on October 28. The Chief Minister said that at least seven people were killed in the cyclone. A preliminary estimate puts the losses caused by the cyclone at Rs 4,600 crore, he said, adding that the figure could increase after a detailed assessment. On October 29, CM Naidu carried out an aerial survey over cyclone-affected areas in the Dr BR Ambedkar Konaseema district. He inspected the relief centres at Gachakayalapora village in Mummidivaram constituency and interacted with cyclone victims. Addressing the media, the CM announced that Central teams would visit the state on October 30 to assess the cyclone damage. He said that he spoke to Union Home Minister Amit Shah about the cyclone situation and the measures taken by the state government, and submitted a preliminary damage report to the Union government. Naidu announced that a compensation of Rs 1,500 will be provided for each damaged coconut tree and each damaged oil palm tree.
